newsitem.title: USA: Hayes Wheels buys Lemmerz of Germany for $245 million.
newsitem.headline: Hayes Wheels buys Lemmerz of Germany for $245 million.

text.p: Hayes Wheels International Inc., looking to extend its dominance in automotive wheels, said Monday it agreed to buy 77 percent of Lemmerz, Europe's leading wheel supplier, for more than $245 million in cash and stock.

Romulus, Mich.-based Hayes, already the largest auto wheel maker in North America, said it will also assume $55 million in Lemmerz' debt. The deal would create a new company with estimated annual sales of $1.5 billion.

The combined company, to be named Hayes Lemmerz International Inc., will be the world's largest supplier of wheels and will also sell brake drums and other parts to virtually every major automaker around the world, Hayes said.

"The combination of two of the oldest and most respected wheel manufacturers in the world will enhance the value we provide our customers because we are establishing a company that is the largest and most experienced supplier of wheels to the automotive and heavy-duty markets worldwide," Hayes Chairman Ron Cucuz said in a statement.
"Together we will supply virtually every major vehicle producer in the world."
The Lemmertz pact, coming five months after Hayes bought Motor Wheel Corp. of Okemos, Mich., for $1.1 billion, is another sign of consolidation in the auto components industry.

Gregory Janicki, vice president of CSM Corp., an industry consultant in Lansing, Mich., said the 22 wheel makers in North America were part of a fragmented industry, with Hayes one of a few companies making both aluminum and steel wheels.
"Hayes basically owns the North American market already," said Janicki.

For 1997 models that went on sale in early autumn, CSM estimated Hayes had 27.8 percent of the total North American wheel market. The next biggest firm was Superior Industries International Inc. of Van Nuys, Calif., which had about 18 percent of the market.

Last week, Hayes said it won a contract to supply cast aluminum wheels for the much-awaited Boxter roadster from Porsche AG. In November, Hayes won a contract to supply chromed steel wheels for the hot-selling 1997 Expedition full-size sport utility from Ford Motor Co.

Hayes has 4,200 employees at manufacturing facilities in the United States, Mexico, Italy, Spain and the Czech Republic, with joint ventures in Venezuela, Japan, Mexico and Brazil. Annual sales including Motor Wheel would have been about $968 million last year.

Lemmerz, based in Konigswinter, Germany, has 3,000 employees at plants in Germany, Spain, Belgium, Switzerland, Netherlands and Turkey. The company, with other ventures in Canada, Thailand, Brazil, India and Portugal, had 1995 sales of about $450 million.

On completion of the transaction, closely held Lemmerz will become a unit of Hayes Lemmerz. Cucuz, 52, will become chairman and chief executive of Hayes Lemmerz International, which will be based in Romulus, a suburb of Detroit.

Under the terms of the deal, Lemmerz stockholders will receive payments of $110 million in cash and Hayes preferred stock convertible into 3.75 million shares of Hayes common stock. Based on Hayes' stock price of $36.50, the stock would be worth about $136.9 million.
Hayes' stock added $1.75 to $36.50 on Nasdaq.
